materials.text:
Every morning, a bird outside my window made a short, clear sound. I wanted to know its name. When our science teacher announced a bird-listening walk, I joined at once. In the park, we heard many calls. I played my recording beside a tree where birds were calling. Our teacher asked us to listen ____3____. The sound from the tree ended with three quick notes. My recording ended with two. Similar beginnings did not make the calls ____4____. Anya drew two little lines and then three beside them to mark the ____5____.

A few minutes later, we heard something much closer to my recording. I looked up, expecting a bird among the leaves. Instead, a man beside the path took a small object from his mouth. He was using a bird ____6____ for a demonstration. She said a sound could have an unexpected ____7____. 

At home, I opened the window the next morning. The familiar call returned, and this time I saw a small bird on the fence. I noted its shape, colours and the time. I did not get a clear photograph because it flew ____8____ before I could lift the phone. The teacher used my notes to suggest two possible species, then showed me what detail would help ____9____ them.
